title: Precedence and evaluation order
summary: *p++, 6 & 3 == 2, and the order C++ doesn't promise.

cards.title: Operators that surprise
cards.body: Postfix `++` binds tighter than `*`, so `*p++` is `*(p++)`. And `==` binds tighter than `&`, so `6 & 3 == 2` is `6 & (3 == 2)`. GCC and Clang warn about the last two with `-Wall`.

cards.question: `int a[] = {1, 2, 3}; int* p = a; int v = *++p;` What is v?
cards.explain: Prefix ++ moves p to a[1] first, then * reads it: 2.

cards.title: Unspecified evaluation order
cards.body: The arguments of a function call may be evaluated in any order. While building this app, two RNG calls inside one `printf` printed their values in reverse, which is exactly this rule. If order matters, use separate statements.

cards.question: `log(next(), next());` Which value does the first parameter receive?
cards.explain: Each argument is evaluated fully, but which one first is up to the compiler. Write `auto a = next(); auto b = next(); log(a, b);`.
